We first determine whether the patient reached age 90; we do not independently cap every day offset with LEAST(offset, 32872).

## Suggested reply
> Hi Dana,
>
> For the 32,872-day top-coding, we first determine whether the patient actually reached age 90, using the relevant birth and event dates. We then apply the top-code only when that age threshold is reached, rather than independently wrapping every day offset in LEAST(offset, 32872).
>
> All the best,
> Alvaro

Two notes:
- This distinction matters because applying LEAST to every offset would look like a blanket numerical cap, whereas the intended rule is tied specifically to whether the patient reached the age-90 threshold.
- If you are checking the implementation, the clearest test cases are dates immediately before and on the patient's 90th birthday, confirming that top-coding begins only at the threshold.

| Scenario | Expected handling |
|---|---|
| Patient is younger than 90 | Keep the calculated day offset |
| Patient has reached age 90 | Apply the 32,872-day top-code |
